To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The performance of Spark is currently limited by the JVM object model and garbage collector; (2) The JVM is not the best choice for the implementation of distributed data analytics systems; and (3) We can improve the performance of distributed data analytics by implementing a distributed data structure, such as a hash table, in a low-level programming language, and by optimizing the memory access of that data structure.
(1) the performance of Spark and Hadoop is bottlenecked by CPU and memory, and (2) the performance of these systems can be improved through the use of in-memory data structures and in-place updates.

We present the design and implementation of a distributed in-memory computing system, called SWAT, which is capable of achieving performance comparable to the fastest distributed in-memory systems, but with significantly less overhead.
